initial_response.topic: Gamma-ray log는 공극률을 직접 재는 도구니까 GR 숫자만으로 공극률이 정확히 확정된다고 보면 되나?
initial_response.goal: Gamma-ray log는 공극률을 직접 재는 도구니까 GR 숫자만으로 공극률이 정확히 확정된다고 보면 되나?
initial_response.final_answer:
Gamma-ray log은 공극률을 직접 재는 도구이다. [KB6]
Gamma-ray log의 측정 결과는 공극률을 직접적으로 결정하는 요소이다. [KB6]
Gamma-ray log의 측정 데이터를 기반으로 공극률을 계산하는 수학적 또는 물리적 모델이 존재한다. [KB6]
Gamma-ray log의 측정 데이터는 공극률을 유일하게 결정하는 요소가 아니라 다른 변수나 조건이 영향을 미칠 수 있다. [KB5]

frozen_criteria.description: Gamma-ray log의 측정 원리와 공극률 측정 방법 간의 관계를 명확히 설명할 수 있는 문서 또는 자료가 존재해야 함.
Gamma-ray log의 측정 결과가 공극률을 직접적으로 결정하는 요소인지에 대한 학술적 또는 엔지니어링적 근거가 제공되어야 함.
Gamma-ray log의 측정 데이터를 기반으로 공극률을 계산하는 수학적 또는 물리적 모델이 존재해야 함.
Gamma-ray log의 측정 데이터가 공극률을 유일하게 결정하는 요소가 아니라 다른 변수나 조건이 영향을 미칠 수 있음을 설명할 수 있는 자료가 존재해야 함.

phistication.  The  energy  of  the  gamma  ray  captured  by  the  detector  is  proportional  to  the
brightness of the light pulse it produces, and this brightness, in turn, determines the size of the

ment emitted them.

Before getting into how to use the log readings, let us consider the workings of the tool.
Unlike  all  other  nuclear tools  (and,  in  fact,  all  other  logging  measurements), it  is  completely
passive. It emits no radiation. Instead, it simply detects incoming gamma rays from the forma-
tion and (unfortunately) the borehole. Gamma rays are electromagnetic radiation, generally in
the energy range 0.1 to 100 MeV. As light, this would correspond to very short wavelengths
indeed. The difference between gamma rays and X-rays is largely semantic because they over-
lap in energy.

cently, the detectors have been switched to solid-state scintillation crystals such as NaI. When

tiplier  shapes  the  light  into  an  electrical  pulse  that  is  counted  by  the  tool.  Hence,  like  all
nuclear  tools,  the  raw  measured  quantity  in  a  gamma  ray  log  is  counts.  As  discussed  above,

4 IDENTIFICATION OF PERMEABLE AND NON-PERMEABLE 	
ZONES FROM LOGS
The permeable zones on a suite of logs can be identified by referring to the GR, SP 
and resistivity logs.  The Gamma Ray log is generally used as a depth reference tool 
and the Gamma Ray sonde is therefore run with all logging tools.  It is however 
primarily used from an interpretation viewpoint to differentiate between shales and 
other formation types.  Since shales generally have a very low permeability (very 
common caprocks) the Gamma Ray log response can be used in a qualitative way 
to identify non-permeable zones.   The technique for identifying permeable zones 
on an SP log is provided in Section 3 of Chapter 4.  A comparison of the resistivity 
readings from the flushed zone, shallow and deep into the reservoir (Figure 3) will 
give some indication of the depth of penetration of the borehole fluid and therefore 
the permeability of the formation.

Log Measurements and Tools
1 INTRODUCTION
The petrophysical properties of the formations through which a borehole has been 
drilled, such as porosity, hydrocarbon saturation and permeability are not measured 
directly with electric wireline logging tools but are inferred from specific measurements 
made on the rocks.  The tools used to make the measurements, and the properties 
which can be inferred or quantified from these measurements will be presented in 
this chapter.
The interpretation of the measurements made by logging tools can only be made reliably 
if the operating principals of the tools and resulting measurements are understood.

Log Measurements and Tools
1 INTRODUCTION
The petrophysical properties of the formations through which a borehole has been 
drilled, such as porosity, hydrocarbon saturation and permeability are not measured 
directly with electric wireline logging tools but are inferred from specific measurements 
made on the rocks.  The tools used to make the measurements, and the properties 
which can be inferred or quantified from these measurements will be presented in 
this chapter.
The interpretation of the measurements made by logging tools can only be made reliably 
if the operating principals of the tools and resulting measurements are understood.

The above list of uncertainties for a given reservoir, especially at the appraisal stage, 
is really quite realistic and is by no means complete.  As we have noted elsewhere, 
it is at the appraisal stage when, although the future reservoir performance is at its 
most uncertain, we must make the biggest decisions about the development and hence 
speed most of our investment money.
